'''Heinz-Dietmar Behnke''' (born 1937), usually published as '''H.-Dietmar Behnke''', is a German [[botanist]] and professor at [[Heidelberg University]]. He is known for using [[transmission electron microscopy]] of the [[plastid]]s found in [[phloem]] [[sieve element]]s as a character in the classification of [[flowering plant]]s, and for his work on the systematics of the [[Caryophyllales]] and the monocot family [[Velloziaceae]].<ref name="gnd">{{cite web |title=Behnke, Heinz-Dietmar |url=https://lobid.org/gnd/1068546360 |website=Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND), via lobid-gnd |publisher=[[German National Library]] |access-date=3 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="heibib">{{cite web |title=Behnke, Heinz-Dietmar |url=https://katalog.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/profil/1068546360 |website=heiBIB |publisher=Heidelberg University Library |access-date=3 October 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==
Behnke has spent his career at Heidelberg University, where he is listed as a professor in the Faculty of Biology.<ref name="gnd" /><ref name="heibib" /> His later publications give his affiliation as the plant cell biology group (Pflanzliche Zellbiologie) of the Centre for Organismal Studies at Heidelberg.<ref name="behnke2013">{{cite journal |last1=Behnke |first1=H.-Dietmar |last2=Hummel |first2=Eric |last3=Hillmer |first3=Stefan |last4=Sauer-Gürth |first4=Hedwig |last5=Gonzalez |first5=Javier |last6=Wink |first6=Michael |title=A revision of African Velloziaceae based on leaf anatomy characters and ''rbcL'' nucleotide sequences |journal=[[Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society]] |year=2013 |volume=172 |issue=1 |pages=22–94 |doi=10.1111/boj.12018}}</ref>

== Research ==
=== Sieve-element plastids ===
Beginning in the late 1960s, Behnke studied the fine structure of plastids in the sieve tubes of flowering plants. In a series of German-language papers he described sieve-tube plastids in groups such as the monocotyledons, the Caryophyllales and the [[Aristolochiaceae]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=Die Siebröhren-Plastiden der Monocotyledonen |journal=Planta |doi=10.1007/BF00398395}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=Über Siebröhren-Plastiden und Plastidenfilamente der Caryophyllales |journal=Planta |doi=10.1007/BF00385032}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=Zum Feinbau der Siebröhren-Plastiden von ''Aristolochia'' und ''Asarum'' (Aristolochiaceae) |journal=Planta |doi=10.1007/BF00388406}}</ref> His review in ''[[The Botanical Review]]'', "Sieve-tube plastids in relation to angiosperm systematics: an attempt towards a classification by ultrastructural analysis", proposed sorting plastids into types, most broadly S-type (starch-accumulating) and P-type (protein-accumulating), and using their distribution as evidence of relationships between plant families.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=Sieve-tube plastids in relation to angiosperm systematics: an attempt towards a classification by ultrastructural analysis |journal=[[The Botanical Review]] |year=1972 |volume=38 |pages=155–197 |doi=10.1007/BF02872355}}</ref> He later extended the survey to the dicotyledons as a whole and to the evolution of the monocotyledons.<ref name="heibib" /><ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=Distribution and evolution of forms and types of sieve-element plastids in the dicotyledons |journal=Aliso |year=1991 |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=167–182 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313645571_Distribution_and_evolution_of_forms_and_types_of_sieve-element_plastids_in_the_dicotyledons}}</ref>

=== Caryophyllales ===
P-type plastids with a characteristic ring of protein filaments became one of the defining features of the Caryophyllales (formerly Centrospermae). With [[Tom J. Mabry]] and others, Behnke used plastid type together with [[betalain]] pigments to place disputed genera such as ''[[Gisekia]]'' and ''[[Dysphania]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mabry |first1=Tom J. |last2=Behnke |first2=H.-Dietmar |title=Betalains and P-type sieve-element plastids in ''Gisekia'' L. (Centrospermae) |journal=[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]] |year=1976 |doi=10.2307/1220417}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mabry |first1=Tom J. |last2=Behnke |first2=H.-Dietmar |title=Betalains and P-type sieve-element plastids: the systematic position of ''Dysphania'' R. Br. (Centrospermae) |journal=[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]] |year=1976 |doi=10.2307/1220416}}</ref> He also reported P-type plastids in tribes of the [[Polygonaceae]], strengthening the link between that family and the Caryophyllales.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Behnke |first=H.-Dietmar |title=P-type sieve-element plastids present in members of the tribes Triplareae and Coccolobeae (Polygonaceae) renew the links between the Polygonales and the Caryophyllales |journal=[[Plant Systematics and Evolution]] |doi=10.1007/BF00985729}}</ref> Behnke and Mabry edited the 1994 Springer volume ''Caryophyllales: Evolution and Systematics'', which brought together molecular, phytochemical, ultrastructural and morphological evidence on the order.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Behnke |editor1-first=H.-Dietmar |editor2-last=Mabry |editor2-first=Tom J. |title=Caryophyllales: Evolution and Systematics |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |year=1994 |isbn=978-3-642-78222-0 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-78220-6}}</ref> In 1997 he named the family [[Sarcobataceae]], segregating the North American genus ''[[Sarcobatus]]'' (greasewood) from the [[Chenopodiaceae]].<ref name="ipni">{{cite web |title=Behnke, H.-Dietmar |url=https://www.ipni.org/a/37730-1 |website=[[International Plant Names Index]] |access-date=3 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sarcobataceae |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?mode=Info&id=91876 |website=NCBI Taxonomy Browser |publisher=[[National Center for Biotechnology Information]] |access-date=3 October 2026}}</ref>

=== Velloziaceae ===
From the late 1990s Behnke turned to the [[Velloziaceae]], a monocot family of drought-tolerant plants in South America, Africa and Madagascar. A 2000 study combining sieve-element plastids with ''[[rbcL]]'' sequence data supported the family as [[monophyletic]] and identified [[Acanthochlamys|Acanthochlamydaceae]] as its sister group.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Behnke |first1=H.-Dietmar |last2=Treutlein |first2=Jens |last3=Wink |first3=Michael |last4=Kramer |first4=Klaus |last5=Schneider |first5=Christian |last6=Kao |first6=P. C. |title=Systematics and evolution of Velloziaceae, with special reference to sieve-element plastids and ''rbcL'' sequence data |journal=[[Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society]] |year=2000 |volume=134 |issue=1–2 |pages=93–129 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.2000.tb02347.x}}</ref> He described ''Xerophyta seinei'' from Zimbabwe in 2002<ref name="heibib" /> and, with colleagues, published a revision of the African Velloziaceae in 2013 based on leaf anatomy and ''rbcL'' sequences, in which several new species of ''[[Xerophyta]]'' were described.<ref name="behnke2013" /><ref name="ipni" />
